title: Geo-aware SLA-driven report dispatcher and resident archive manifest
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Goal: Ship a tenant-scoped dispatcher that produces scheduled PDF/CSV reporting bundles and an accompanying resident archive manifest (signed, checksummed) while enforcing per-tenant residency and retention policies. This ticket covers the product acceptance criteria, edge case behaviors, and rollout constraints for the first-phase implementation targeted at regulated customers that require SLA-driven delivery and verifiable proofs of transmission.

Background: Customers have asked for a single mechanism to schedule compliance snapshots (daily/weekly/monthly), receive human-readable PDFs plus machine-friendly CSVs, and obtain a compact signed manifest that proves the bundle was produced under the requested residency and retention policy. Existing exports are ad-hoc and either miss residency metadata or rely on ad-hoc post-processing.

Scope for phase 1:
- Scheduled jobs per-tenant with timezone-aware cron and tenant SLA window (e.g., within 24 hours of schedule).
- Bundles contain: metadata.json (minimal), data.csv (tabular evidence), summary.pdf (human-readable executive summary), and manifest.sig (base64 signature + checksums).
- Residency routing: if tenant residency = EU, all data extraction and bundle assembly must run in EU-only worker pool; manifest records worker region, processing start/end timestamps, and KMS key id used to sign.
- Retention enforcement: bundle generation respects tenant retention settings (redact or exclude records outside retention window).
- Delivery options: object storage upload in tenant’s residency bucket + webhook notice; optional email delivery for labeled contacts (opt-in).
- Proof-of-delivery: signed manifest + webhook with signed URL and delivery receipt stored as an audit event.

Trade-offs and non-goals:
- We will not implement full multi-tenant aggregation across regions in phase 1 (will be addressed in phase 2).
- No UI for custom template edits in phase 1; templates are set defaults (standard summary layout).
- For very large bundles, we will split into chunked manifests rather than streaming individual files to end users synchronously.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria field)

Links: design doc, API drafts, and example manifests are attached in design_links.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can create and run tenant-scoped jobs with timezone and SLA window; logs show job started within SLA at least 99% of the time in internal load tests.

Generated bundle includes metadata.json, data.csv, summary.pdf and manifest.sig with SHA256 checksums; manifest.sig must validate using tenant KMS public key (or platform verification key if tenant key not configured).
Bundles for tenants with residency set to a region are generated only on workers tagged for that region (testable with worker annotations and audit logs).

Retention rules applied during extraction: records older than tenant retention are redacted or excluded according to tenant setting; random sample verification script demonstrates >99% compliance in staging datasets.
Delivery pipeline uploads bundle to the tenant residency bucket and posts webhook with signed URL and delivery receipt; receipt is persisted as an audit event visible in Console trace for the job.

When a residency pool is unavailable, fallback behavior is exercised per policy: either (a) postpone and retry with exponential backoff (default), or (b) route to backup region with explicit audit note and masking applied. Behavior must be configurable per-tenant.
risks: KMS signing latency in remote regions may push bundle completion past SLA windows; mitigation: pre-warm signing connections and measure latency metrics.
Large exports may incur high egress and storage costs; mitigation: support chunking and optional tenant opt-in for compressed archives.
Incorrect retention enforcement could expose out-of-scope data; mitigation: add sampling tests, retention unit tests, and a soft-blocker gating security review.
testing_plan: Unit tests for extraction/redaction logic; integration tests against regional worker pools; staging job runs with synthetic tenants covering EU/US/APAC residency; automated verification script validates manifest signatures and checksums. Load test to measure scheduler throughput and 99th percentile completion time under expected pilot load.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind pilot tenant list. 2) Canary run for 5 pilot tenants for 48 hours, monitor dashboards and delivery receipts. 3) Expand to pilot cohort (~25 tenants) and run for 2 weeks. 4) Flip default on for tenants with compliance export opt-in. Backout: disable scheduler and mark jobs failed if signature verification error rate > 0.5% for a rolling hour.
review_feedback: Security: require design review due to cross-region signing and KMS usage (see security_review_required). - Nisha Rao
Engineering: prefer asynchronous chunked upload to avoid long-lived worker threads; add job-level heartbeat entries in audit logs. - Leo Park
Design/PM: provide clear Console copy that explains 'signed manifest' and 'residency bucket' to reduce support tickets. - Priya Singh
notes: Follow-on work (phase 2) will add UI scheduling templates, tenant-driven masking policies, and cross-tenant deduped exports for aggregated regulatory reporting. Keep implementation extensible: manifest schema must be versioned and backwards compatible.
communication: Notify pilot customers via direct outreach and include sample manifest verification script in the pilot onboarding kit. Coordinate with Sales and Solutions Engineering to offer a one-time setup call for tenant KMS onboarding.
postmortem_plan: If we observe missed SLAs or signature verification regressions, open a postmortem within 48 hours, include job traces, worker pool health, and KMS metrics; propose compensating controls (re-run, PII review) as immediate remediation.
